title: Disagreement-Gated Judge KV Reuse: A Training-Free Safety Signal for Multi-Agent LLM Systems

contributions.purpose: Provide a training-free safety signal to preserve LLM-judge consistency when KV cache reuse is used to accelerate multi-agent inference.
contributions.mechanism: DG-JKR runs two structurally different KV reuse methods (Naive Reuse and KVCOMM) in parallel and gates on their disagreement, accepting the winner when they agree and falling back to dense prefill when they disagree.
contributions.evaluation: On HumanEval with Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct, DG-JKR reaches 74.38% Judge Consistency Rate, +8.13pp over Naive Reuse; methods agree on 83% of cases.
contributions.domain: Multi-agent LLM judge inference / KV cache reuse
contributions.source_quote: We propose DG-JKR, a training-free method that uses disagreement between KV reuse methods as a safety signal for LLM judges in multi-agent systems.

contributions.purpose: Demonstrate that algorithmic disagreement is a genuinely informative uncertainty signal rather than an arbitrary gating heuristic.
contributions.mechanism: Compares the disagreement gate against a random gating baseline holding fallback rate constant.
contributions.evaluation: Disagreement gating beats random gating by +5.63 percentage points with p < 0.05.
contributions.source_quote: We demonstrate that the disagreement gate is statistically significantly better than random gating (+5.63 percentage points, p < 0.05), confirming that disagreement is an informative uncertainty signal.

contributions.purpose: Show the mechanism generalizes across different candidate generation regimes.
contributions.mechanism: Evaluates DG-JKR under both Progressive Refinement and Parallel Exploration candidate-generation settings.
contributions.evaluation: Achieves consistent improvements in both regimes; reports stable functional improvements of 80.00% +/- 0.62%.
contributions.source_quote: We show that DG-JKR generalizes across candidate generation regimes, achieving consistent improvements in both Progressive Refinement and Parallel Exploration settings.

contributions.purpose: Characterize the cost-consistency tradeoff of the method honestly, including its overhead.
contributions.mechanism: Comprehensive cost-consistency analysis quantifying latency incurred by dual-method execution and dense fallback.
contributions.evaluation: Acknowledges a 4.6x latency overhead while demonstrating significant consistency gains.
contributions.source_quote: We provide comprehensive cost-consistency tradeoff analysis, honestly acknowledging the 4.6x latency overhead while demonstrating significant consistency gains.

self_declared_provenance.quote: Our work builds on these foundations but focuses specifically on the reliability of KV reuse for LLM judges, using disagreement between reuse methods as a safety signal.

Our disagreement-gating mechanism is conceptually related but uses algorithmic diversity rather than sampling diversity: we run two structurally different KV reuse methods (Naive concatenation and KVCOMM) and use their disagreement as an uncertainty signal. This approach requires no additional sampling and provides a training-free safety mechanism that can be applied at inference time without model modification.
Our approach addresses this reliability concern by detecting when KV reuse methods disagree, using this disagreement as a training-free signal to trigger fallback to dense computation.
